editorial:
Imagine being so rich that you are completely bored with your own life. That is where you find the main character, a wealthy woman who spends her days looking for new thrills. She meets a poor young artist on the street and decides to take her to a fancy villa in Saint Tropez. It feels like a dream vacation at first, but things get messy fast. Once they meet a handsome architect in town, the vibe shifts from a friendly mentorship to a weird game of love and lies. You will feel the tension as these three people try to play each other, making it feel more like a psychological game than a typical romance.

The acting is top-notch, especially the way the lead actress shows her cold side. You might find the pacing a bit slow in some spots, but the twists keep you interested. It is a great pick if you like stories about rich people acting badly. It is a stylish trip back to the sixties that still feels fresh today.
endingExplained: The movie ends with a cold realization. After a lot of lying and fighting over the architect, the wealthy woman realizes she cannot actually own or control the young artist. The young woman eventually leaves her, breaking the cycle of dependence. It wraps up by showing that money cannot buy real love or loyalty. You see the rich woman left alone in her big house, proving that her games only led to more loneliness.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about toxic relationships and high-society drama.
